page: Vultr vhf-16c-58gb is a virtual server within the High Frequency Compute family, built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. The instance is provisioned with 58.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.62 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 1024 GB NVMe SSD for local storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard computational and database tasks, with some specific limitations. The server achieves average scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU evaluations, and Redis SET operations. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable strength, registering in the top tier of tested systems. Conversely, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak for reads and poor for writes. Static web serving throughput and PassMark physics simulations also fall into the lower performance categories.

Given its shared CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this server represents a resource-dense option for workloads requiring significant local storage without demanding sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, file compression pipelines, and moderate database operations, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive large-block processing or high-throughput web serving.
